AdaptHealth
supplies home medical equipment, including continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) systems like the Simplera Sync and Dexcom devices, which bridge clinical care with at-home tracking
. While consumer smartwatches and wearables track fitness, sleep, and ECGs, medical-grade remote patient monitoring (RPM) relies on specific cellular or Bluetooth devices linked to provider networks.

AdaptHealth Diabetes & CGM Offerings
Provides in-network continuous glucose monitors, transmitters, and dedicated handheld readers.
Offers devices like the Simplera Sync sensor for the Medtronic 780G system.
Replaces routine fingersticks with real-time interstitial fluid tracking and trend alerts.
Smartwatches and Consumer Wearables
Wearable ECG & PPG:
Consumer watches track heart electrical rhythms and blood oxygen, though they differ from clinical diagnostic ECGs.
Sleep Trackers:
Rings and bands monitor recovery, heart rate variability, and sleep stages.
Blood Glucose Claims:
While some smartwatches claim non-invasive glucose tracking, regulatory bodies caution that they are for general wellness only and not approved for medical treatment decisions.

Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM)
Uses connected medical devices (blood pressure cuffs, glucometers, scales) to transmit vital signs to care teams.
Supports chronic disease management for conditions like diabetes and hypertension outside clinical settings.
Integrates regular data streams into electronic health records for physician review and insurance billing compliance.
